Meet your daily goal for 7 consecutive days
100 hours of good posture or a special health-education achievement
Deep in the forest, a bright-eyed hatchling follows your light. After a long time staring at a screen, the imaginary mist of fatigue hides its path. You decide to help it find a clearing.
Your first spell: blink naturally and pause when your eyes feel tired.
The little dragon opens its wings, but the branches are too close. You move back and give it a comfortable place to fly. A little space makes the journey easier.
For a computer screen, sit about an arm’s length away. Enlarge small text instead of leaning closer.
At a quiet clearing, the dragon needs somewhere to rest. You relax your shoulders and sit comfortably upright. In the story, a steady tree becomes its favorite perch.
Gently tuck your chin, relax your shoulders and support your back. Change position regularly; do not hold a rigid pose.
Beyond the clearing, distant hills sparkle. You look away from the screen with your dragon. While your eyes take a break, stars gather gently around its wings.
20-20-20: every 20 minutes, look about 6 metres (20 feet) away for at least 20 seconds.

With regular breaks and comfortable posture, the forest adventure continues. In your imagination, your companion grows radiant horns and wide wings. It reminds you that caring for yourself is the greatest magic.
Keep the three promises: comfortable distance, relaxed supported posture, and regular eye breaks.
